summary: This PR refactors Vertagus v1.0.0 to unify the rule configuration model. Rules are now declared as a flat list instead of separate `current`/`increment` buckets, with automatic detection of rule types based on class hierarchy. The change simplifies configuration while maintaining backward compatibility through the unified rule registry system.

steps.title: Unified rule base hierarchy
steps.narrative: The refactor begins with establishing a **unified rule class hierarchy** that replaces the previous fragmented approach. The new `Rule` base class provides common functionality including config management and hashing, while `SingleVersionRule` and `ComparisonRule` are concrete base classes for the two main rule categories [1]. This hierarchy enables **automatic rule type detection** at runtime rather than requiring explicit configuration buckets.

refs.heading: Validation Rules
refs.excerpt: Rules are defined as a flat list. Vertagus automatically detects whether each rule validates a single version (e.g., format checks) or compares versions (e.g., increment checks).

steps.title: Centralized rule registry
steps.narrative: Building on the unified hierarchy, the new **rule registry** consolidates all rule discovery into a single system [1]. Instead of maintaining separate loaders for different rule types, `get_all_rules()` pulls from both single-version and comparison rule packages, creating one unified name-to-class mapping. The `get_rule_category()` function automatically classifies rules by their class inheritance, eliminating the need for configuration-time type annotations.

steps.title: Flattened configuration schema
steps.narrative: The configuration types are dramatically simplified with the new **flat rule model**. `RulesConfig` transforms from a complex nested structure with `current`, `increment`, and `manifest_comparisons` buckets into a simple `list[Union[str, TypeAndConfig]]` [1]. The `RulesData` class follows suit, storing rules as a single list instead of separate categorized fields. This represents the core architectural shift toward **declarative simplicity**.

steps.title: Smart rule factory with auto-classification
steps.narrative: The new `create_rules()` factory function is the **heart of the unified system** [1]. It parses the flat rule list, instantiates each rule (handling both string names and configurable `{type, config}` objects), then **automatically sorts instances** into single-version, comparison, or manifest-comparison buckets based on their class types [2][3]. This eliminates the need for users to manually categorize rules while maintaining the internal separation needed by the validation logic.

steps.title: Rule implementations adapt to instance-based model
steps.narrative: The rule implementations shift from **class-based validation** to **instance-based validation**. Single-version rules now implement `validate_version()` as instance methods rather than class methods, and configurable rules like `CustomRegexRule` properly inherit from `SingleVersionRule` with config initialization [1]. The comparison rules similarly adopt the unified `ComparisonRule` base class while maintaining their validation logic.

steps.title: Project and stage models adopt unified rules
steps.narrative: The core domain models update to work with the new rule architecture. `Project` and `Stage` constructors now accept separate lists of `SingleVersionRule` and `ComparisonRule` instances rather than mixed rule collections [1]. The internal accessor methods like `_get_current_version_rules()` return properly typed rule lists, maintaining **type safety** while working with the unified rule instances. This preserves the existing validation API while leveraging the simplified configuration.

refs.excerpt:

    - regex_mmp             # Validates current version matches semver format
    - any_increment         # Validates version is greater than previous

steps.title: CLI commands leverage unified registry
steps.narrative: The CLI adapts to the unified model with **streamlined rule discovery**. The `list-rules` command now uses the central registry to display all available rules with their automatically detected types [1], replacing the previous approach of querying separate rule loaders. This provides users with a **single source of truth** for understanding available validation rules and their categories.

refs.heading: `vertagus list-rules`
refs.excerpt:
### `vertagus list-rules`

Display all available validation rules.

```bash
vertagus list-rules
```

steps.title: Configuration generation reflects new schema
steps.narrative: The `init` command generates configuration files using the **flattened rule syntax** [1]. Instead of creating nested `current` and `increment` sections, it outputs a simple list like `["not_empty", "regex_mmp", "any_increment"]`. Stage configurations similarly use flat rule lists, making the generated configs immediately aligned with the new documentation examples while maintaining all the same validation capabilities.

steps.title: Documentation showcases simplified configuration
steps.narrative: The configuration documentation transforms to highlight the **flat rule model** [1]. Examples now show rules as simple lists rather than nested structures, demonstrating stage-specific rules, configurable rules with `type`/`config` syntax [2], and manifest comparison rules [3]. The documentation emphasizes that **Vertagus automatically detects rule types**, removing the cognitive burden of manual categorization from users.

steps.title: Comprehensive test suite adaptation
steps.narrative: The test suite undergoes **extensive adaptation** to the unified model. Mock rule classes become instance-based, test fixtures provide properly typed rule lists, and factory tests verify that the new `create_rules()` function correctly parses flat rule configurations and sorts instances into the right categories. The tests ensure that both simple rule names and configurable `{type, config}` objects work correctly, validating the **backward compatibility** of the refactor.

steps.title: Real-world configuration migration
steps.narrative: The Vertagus project's own configuration demonstrates the **practical migration path** [1]. The `vertagus.yaml` transforms from nested rule buckets to a clean flat list: `["not_empty", "any_increment"]` at the project level, with stage-specific rules like `["regex_dev_mmp"]` and `["regex_mmp"]` [2]. This real-world example shows how the refactor **simplifies configuration** while maintaining all the same validation capabilities that ensure development and production version formats are properly enforced.
